units.translation: [The perfect is βέβηκα [I have gone] (Doric βέβακα [I have gone]), third person plural βεβᾶσι [they have gone], participle βεβώς [having gone]. The aorist is ἔβην [I went] (Doric ἔβαν [I went]), with third person plural ἔβαν [they went], Pers. 18 (the second syllable lengthened in anapaests before punctuation), imperative βᾶτε [go!], infinitive βῆναι [to go], participle βάς [having gone], plural βᾶσαι [having gone (fem.)].]
The perfect βέβηκα [I have gone] often has the meaning of the present: I am, I am situated
they have gone away, i.e. they have perished.

to throw, to cast, to strike

(with perfect βέβληκα [I have thrown], aorist ἔβαλον [I threw], future βαλῶ [I will throw]) I throw, I hurl, I strike. It is used either properly of things that are thrown, or improperly of things that strike the senses.

which can be said by tmesis for ἀμφίβαλε [throw around], as Ag. 1559 περὶ χεῖρε βαλοῦσα φιλήσει [having thrown her arms around, she will kiss] for περιβαλοῦσα [having embraced], and Ch. 395 καὶ πότ᾽ ἂν ἀμφιθαλὴς Ζεὺς ἐπὶ χεῖρα βάλοι [and when would flourishing Zeus lay his hand upon] for ἐπιβάλοι [lay upon], and 574 καὶ κατ᾿ ὀφθαλμοὺς βαλεῖ [and will cast down over the eyes] for καταβαλεῖ [cast down].
which is the highest throw in the game of dice: see under the word τρίς [three].
